rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theoretical beliefs are not acquired: if they necessarily follow involuntary first principles, they too are involuntary; if not, those principles cannot prove them, leaving imitation rather than knowledge.
rows.anchor: التصديقات بأسرها غير كسبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ambiguous revelations tip motives toward error, the resulting necessity entails compulsion, contrary to the opponents’ account of misguidance.
rows.anchor: إذا أثر إنزال هذه المتشابهات في الترجيح وثبت أنه متى حصل الترجيح فقد حصل الوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even short of necessity, revelations that incline a person toward error excuse failure to obey, making their divinely sent effect blameworthy on this account.
rows.anchor: لها أثرا في ترجيح جانب الضلال على جانب الاهتداء كالعذر للمكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the ambiguous verses have no effect on choice, they are as irrelevant to misguidance as a door creaking or a crow calling, so cannot explain it.
rows.anchor: كانت نسبة هذه المتشابهات إلى ضلالهم كصرير الباب ونعيق الغراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s naming and judging someone misguided would make noncompliance impossible, since otherwise God’s truthful report and knowledge would become false and ignorant.
rows.anchor: إذا سماه الله بذلك وحكم به عليه فلو لم يأت المكلف به لانقلب خبر الله الصدق كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling divine non-prevention misguidance fails: a parent is not said to mislead a child when preventing one harm would cause a greater one, as divine prevention would here.
rows.anchor: لو منع المكلف جبرا عن هذه المفسدة لزمت مفسدة أخرى أعظم من الأولى

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Qaffal rejects equating misguidance with punishment: in 54:47 the criminals err from truth, while “in burning” refers to their later punishment.
rows.anchor: اعتراض القفال عليه فقال : لا نسلم بأن الضلال جاء بمعنى العذاب

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Qaffal reads “they strayed from us” in 40:50 as becoming useless, then offers either destruction of their deeds or God’s forsaking them in worldly life for “misguides the disbelievers.”
rows.anchor: كذلك يضل الله أعمالهم أي يحبطها يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguidance as destruction does not fit because the contrasting statement says that God guides many through the same verses.
rows.anchor: التأويل الخامس : وهو الإهلاك فغير لائق بهذا الموضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguidance as barring the way to Paradise is weak: “through it” ties error to hearing the verses, whereas exclusion from Paradise follows sinful acts.
rows.anchor: وأما التأويل السادس : وهو أنه يضله عن طريق الجنة فضعيف لأنه تعالى قال : { يضل به }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreting “misguides” as “finds astray” lacks linguistic evidence and conflicts with the verb’s use with the preposition bi.
rows.anchor: عدى الإضلال بحرف الباء فقال : { يضل به } والإضلال بمعنى الوجدان لا يكون معدى بحرف الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the first half of the clause unbelievers’ speech and the second God’s speech fractures the syntax; 74:31 also plainly attributes “misguides whom He wills” to God.
rows.anchor: إلى قوله يضل به كثيرا ويهدي به كثيرا من كلام الكفار ثم قوله : { وما يضل به إلا الفاسقين } كلام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance can mean disclosure and proof; Qur’anic examples show unbelievers received guidance through signs, revelation, and the prophets’ explanations.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الدلالة والبيان قال تعالى : { أو لم * يهد لهم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: A second sense is invitation or calling: the Prophet guides by calling people, and every people has a caller toward error or guidance.
rows.anchor: قالوا في قوله : { عبادنا وإنك لتهدى إلى صراط مستقيم }

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: A third sense is God’s enabling grace, given to believers as reward for faith and help toward further obedience; withholding its counterpart from unbelievers is misguidance.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : التوفيق من الله بالألطاف المشروطة بالإيمان

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The cited cases where people have received proofs but God does not guide them show that this guidance is distinct from disclosure and proof.
rows.anchor: فأخبر أنه لا يهديهم وأنهم قد جاءهم البينات ، فهذا الهدى غير البيان

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: A fourth sense is guidance to Paradise, supported by verses that link guidance with entry into Paradise and the paths of peace.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : الهدى إلى طريق الجنة قال تعالى : { فأما الذين ءامنوا بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth sense is putting someone forward, from the guide who goes ahead of the one being led; Arabic calls the foremost parts of a horse train its hawadi.
rows.anchor: وهذا تأويل الجبائي ، وخامسها : الهدى بمعنى التقديم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: A sixth sense is God’s ruling or naming someone guided; scripture uses “make” for legal designation and “God’s guidance” for what He judges guidance.
rows.anchor: وسادسها : يهدي أي يحكم بأن المؤمن مهتد وتسميته بذلك

rows.speaker: الجبرية
rows.claim: The determinists add that guidance means God’s creation of guidance and knowledge in a person.
rows.anchor: قالت الجبرية : وههنا وجه آخر وهو أن يكون الهدى بمعنى خلق الهداية والعلم

rows.speaker: القدرية
rows.claim: The Qadarites object that forcibly making someone take a path is called driving or dragging him, not guiding him.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يصح في اللغة أن يقال لمن حمل غيره على سلوك الطريق كرها وجبرا أنه هداه إليه

rows.speaker: القدرية
rows.claim: They argue that if God creates the act, commands, prohibitions, praise, blame, reward, and punishment lose their basis; the proposed human acquisition cannot restore real ability.
rows.anchor: لو حصل ذلك بخلق الله تعالى لبطل الأمر والنهي والمدح والذم والثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: القدرية
rows.claim: They further argue that acquisition cannot precede or follow God’s creation, and simultaneous creation and acquisition would require an infinite regress of prior agreements.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فهذا الاتفاق وجب أن لا يحصل إلا باتفاق آخر ، لأنه من كسبه وفعله

rows.speaker: الجبرية
rows.claim: The determinists answer that decisive rational proofs establish God as creator of all acts, while the Qadarites’ textual arguments admit interpretation, so the rational proofs prevail.
rows.anchor: على أن خالق هذه الأفعال هو الله تعالى ، إما بواسطة أو بغير واسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guided people may be many in absolute number but few relative to those astray; the genuinely few may also be called many in reality despite their outward scarcity.
rows.anchor: والجواب : أهل الهدى كثير في أنفسهم وحيث يوصفون بالقلة إنما يوصفون بها بالقياس إلى أهل الضلال

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra’ derives fisq from a date escaping its shell: a fasiq is one who exits obedience, while a mouse is called fuwaysiqa for emerging to cause harm.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : الفاسق أصله من قولهم فسقت الرطبة من قشرها

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The author’s theological school counts a sinner as a believer; the Kharijites call him an unbeliever, while the Mu‘tazilites place him between belief and unbelief.
rows.anchor: فعند أصحابنا أنه مؤمن ، وعند الخوارج أنه كافر ، وعند المعتزلة أنه لا مؤمن ولا كافر

rows.speaker: المخالف
rows.claim: Opponents cite “the name of wickedness after faith,” the description of hypocrites as sinners, and the contrast between faith and fisq to argue that a fasiq is not a believer.
rows.anchor: بئس الاسم الفسوق بعد الايمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is breaking kinship ties and relatives’ rights; it may specifically allude to severing the family relationship with the Prophet, but that makes the verse particular.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن المراد بهذا الميثاق حججه القائمة على عباده الدالة لهم على صحة توحيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation identifies the covenant as a vow by some people to follow a warner if one came; their refusal would breach it, but this applies only to those who swore.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : يحتمل أن يعني به ما دل عليه بقوله : { وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the first, general reading because it avoids restricting the verse and grounds blame in rejecting God’s repeatedly established proofs in creation, reason, scripture, and prophecy.
rows.anchor: رجحان التأويل الأول على الثاني من وجهين : الأول : أن على التقدير الأول يمكن إجراء الآية

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Qaffal suggests the verse concerns People of the Book who broke scriptural pledges to affirm Muhammad, his message, and his community.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : قال القفال : يحتمل أن يكون المقصود بالآية قوما من أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify the covenant with humanity’s primordial pledge; theologians reject this because people cannot fairly be blamed for a pact they do not remember.
rows.anchor: ورابعا : قال بعضهم ، إنه عنى به ميثاقا أخذه من الناس وهم على صورة الذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further account distinguishes three covenants: Adam’s descendants acknowledge God’s lordship, prophets promise to convey revelation and uphold one religion, and scholars promise to clarify scripture rather than conceal it.
rows.anchor: وخامسها : عهد الله إلى خلقه ثلاثة عهود

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says “His covenant” can refer to the covenant they accepted, its ratification, or God, who reinforced it through signs, books, and messengers.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : الضمير في ميثاقه للعهد وهو ما وثقوا به عهد الله من قبوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is severing kinship and relatives’ rights, possibly alluding specifically to cutting family ties with the Prophet; this makes the verse particular.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أراد به قطيعة الرحم وحقوق القرابات التي أمر الله بوصلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation is severing ties with believers while joining oneself to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أن الله تعالى أمرهم أن يصلوا حبلهم بحبل المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation is the dissent and strife they pursued despite being forbidden to quarrel and stir up discord.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أنهم نهوا عن التنازع وإثارة الفتن وهم كانوا مشتغلين بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest sense of corruption is harm extending beyond its perpetrator, especially obstructing obedience to the Messenger; observance of the law establishes justice and social order.
rows.anchor: فالأظهر أن يراد به الفساد الذي يتعدى دون ما يقف عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi connects opposition to the Messenger with social corruption, citing Pharaoh’s fear that changing religion would spread corruption in the land.
rows.anchor: إنى أخاف أن يبدل دينكم أو أن يظهر فى الارض الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account of their loss is forfeiting their place in Paradise: each person has a place there, which the obedient attain and believers inherit from the disobedient.
rows.anchor: أنه لا أحد إلا وله في الجنة أهل ومنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second account is that unbelief cancels the good deeds of Jews and hypocrites, leaving no benefit or reward from those deeds.
rows.anchor: خسروا حسناتهم التي عملوها لأنهم أحبطوها بكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third account is that they clung to unbelief to preserve immediate pleasures, only to lose them when fighting was permitted or when they died.
rows.anchor: إنما أصروا على الكفر خوفا من أن تفوتهم اللذات العاجلة

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Qaffal defines loss generally as work that brings no recompense, like spending effort and receiving nothing of equal value; he links this to other verses about futile labor.
rows.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله تعالى : وبالجملة أن الخاسر اسم عام يقع على كل من عمل عملا لا يجزي عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi’ and Ibn Amir read awṣā with an alif, as in Medina and Syrian codices; the others read waṣṣā with gemination, suggesting emphasis and repetition though the meaning is alike.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر ( وأوصى ) بالألف وكذلك هو في مصاحف المدينة والشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to Abraham’s statement “I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds,” understood as a word or sentence; the feminine form is supported by “a word enduring.”
rows.anchor: أنه عائد إلى قوله : { أسلمت لرب العالمين } ( البقرة : 131 ) على تأويل الكلمة

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi prefers that the pronoun refer to Abraham’s religion: it has an explicit antecedent and is broader than a single profession of faith, encompassing what secures success in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي وهذا القول أولى من الأول من وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it a testament rather than an order makes the charge more emphatic because concern for religion intensifies as death approaches.
rows.anchor: لفظ الوصية أوكد من الأمر ، لأن الوصية عند الخوف من الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham addressed his sons because a father’s care for them is especially strong, showing how seriously he regarded the faith.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن شفقة الرجل على أبنائه أكثر من شفقته على غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He included all his sons without exception, which further signals his intense concern.
rows.anchor: عمم بهذه الوصية جميع بنيه ولم يخص أحدا منهم بهذه الوصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbounded command and prohibition against dying outside Islam require constant adherence, since death may come at any moment.
rows.anchor: أطلق هذه الوصية غير مقيدة بزمان معين ومكان معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham included no other testament, signaling that this was his foremost concern; although he specially addressed family, he invited all people to Islam.
rows.anchor: ما مزج بهذه الوصية وصية أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read “and Jacob” as coordinated with Abraham, meaning Jacob gave the same testament; an accusative reading coordinates it with “his sons” and includes his grandson Jacob in Abraham’s testament.
rows.anchor: الأول : وهو الأشهر أنه معطوف على إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative “O my sons” is an implied quotation for Basran grammarians and governed by “testament” as a speech act for Kufans; Ubayy and Ibn Masud read it with the particle ya.
rows.anchor: فهو على إضمار القول عند البصريين ، وعند الكوفيين يتعلق بوصي لأنه في معنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose the religion by establishing clear proofs, calling them to it, and keeping them from other religions.
rows.anchor: استخلصه بأن أقام عليه الدلائل الظاهرة الجلية ودعاكم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to die except as Muslims requires embracing Islam at every moment, because death may arrive before a person later turns to it.
rows.anchor: إذا لم يأمن الموت في كل طرفة عين ، ثم إنه أمر بأن يأتي بالشيء قبل الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Jacob’s testament follows Abraham’s to reinforce the proof against Jews and Christians and make the case clearer.
rows.anchor: ذكر عقيبه أن يعقوب وصى بنيه بمثل ذلك تأكيدا للحجة على اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle am may be connected or disconnected: connected am asks which of two alternatives is true, while disconnected am means “rather” plus a question and abandons the prior assertion.
rows.anchor: وأما المنقطعة فقالوا : إنها بمعنى ( بل ) مع همزة الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The connected form asks which of two known alternatives applies; unlike the disconnected form, its second option stays linked to the first and can be restated as “which one?”
rows.anchor: ولم يكن ( ما ) بعد ( أم ) منقطعا عما قبله بدليل أن عمرا قرين زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’anic examples distinguish connected am in 79:27 from disconnected am in 32:1–3, where “rather, do they say he fabricated it?” rejects the prior assertion; treating it as a bare hamza is mistaken.
rows.anchor: ومن لا يحقق من المفسرين يقولون إن ( أم ) ههنا بمنزلة الهمزة وذلك غير صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Witnesses” means people present; the address challenges the People of the Book, whose claim to follow the prophets conflicts with the prophets’ call to Islam and Muhammad’s same religion.
rows.anchor: ( والشهداء ) جمع شهيد بمعنى الحاضر أي ما كنتم حاضرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the disconnected reading, the rebuke targets only the false claim that the addressees were present at Jacob’s death; the quoted testament itself is true and is then explained.
rows.anchor: الاستفهام على سبيل الإنكار متعلق بمجرد ادعائهم الحضور عند وفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the connected reading, an omitted question asks whether they claim the prophets were Jews or were present at Jacob’s death; Israel’s ancestors saw his call to Islam and monotheism.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : في أن ( أم ) في هذه الآية متصلة ، وطريق ذلك أن يقدر قبلها محذوف

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Qaffal says the first “when” marks the time of the alleged witnesses, while the second marks the time Jacob was present at death.
rows.anchor: قال القفال قوله : { إذ حضر يعقوب الموت إذ قال لبنيه } أن ( إذ ) الأولى وقت الشهداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that the prophets’ solicitude for their children centered on religion.
rows.anchor: الآية دالة على أن شفقة الأنبياء عليهم السلام على أولادهم كانت في باب الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative ma can be general—“what thing do you worship?”—or a request for definition, like asking “what is a human?”
rows.anchor: أن ( ما ) عام في كل شيء والمعنى أي شيء تعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the verse proves neither that Jacob’s sons knew God by rational argument nor that they accepted Him only through imitation and instruction.
rows.anchor: كما أنه ليس في الآية دلالة على أنهم عرفوا الإله بالدليل العقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since exclusive reliance on imitation or instruction is disproved, the sons’ faith must have been grounded in reasoning.
rows.anchor: ثم إن القول بالتقليد والتعليم لما بطل بالدليل علمنا أن إيمان القوم ما كان على هذه الطريقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse proves neither rational proof nor exclusive dependence on imitation and instruction; since those exclusive paths are disproved, the sons’ faith must rest on reasoning.
rows.anchor: فليس فيها أيضا دلالة على أنهم ما أقروا بالإله إلا على طريقة التقليد والتعليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They omitted a full exposition of God’s unity, knowledge, power, and justice for brevity.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك أخصر في القول من شرح صفات الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wording reassured Jacob that they followed his own path and would worship God alone without opposing him.
rows.anchor: لسنا نجري إلا على مثل طريقتك فلا خلاف منا عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reference to the God of Jacob and the ancestors may point to the rational proof in 2:21: the creator demonstrated by their existence.
rows.anchor: وههنا مرادهم بقولهم : { نعبد إلاهك وإلاه آبائك } أي : نعبد الإله الذي دل عليه وجودك

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Qaffal relates that Jacob saw Egyptians worshipping fire and idols and questioned his sons out of fear for their faith.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : وفي بعض التفاسير أن يعقوب عليه السلام لما دخل مصر رأى أهلها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Qadi reports Ibn Abbas’s story that Jacob gathered his sons at death while they worshipped idols and fire and asked what they would worship after him.
rows.anchor: وحكى القاضي عن ابن عباس : أن يعقوب عليه السلام جمعهم إليه عند الوفاة

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi calls that story unlikely: the sons’ prompt monotheistic answer implies settled knowledge, and the Qur’an describes Jacob’s descendants as righteous.
rows.anchor: هذا بعيد لوجهين . الأول : أنهم بادروا إلى الاعتراف بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Qaffal treats Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac as an appositional explanation of “your fathers”; Ishmael precedes Isaac because he was older.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : وقيل أنه قدم ذكر إسماعيل على إسحاق لأن إسماعيل كان أسن من إسحاق

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Shafi‘i, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Ibn Mas‘ud, Zayd, Malik, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad hold that full or paternal siblings are not excluded from inheritance by a grandfather.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : الأخوة والأخوات للأب والأم أو للأب لا يسقطون بالجد

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa, Abu Bakr, Ibn Abbas, Aisha, and several Successors hold that a grandfather excludes siblings from inheritance.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة : إنهم يسقطون بالجد

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Among those who do not let a grandfather exclude siblings, Zayd and Shafi‘i give him the better of sharing with them or one-third of the estate, then divide the remainder among siblings, males receiving twice females.
rows.anchor: أن الجد خير الأمرين : إما المقاسمة معهم أو ثلث جميع المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second non-exclusion rule treats the grandfather as one of the siblings unless that would reduce his share below one-sixth, in which case he receives one-sixth.
rows.anchor: أنه بمنزلة أحد الأخوة ما لم تنقصه المقاسمة من السدس

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa argues that this verse calls a grandfather “father,” and Joseph’s statement about the religion of his fathers does likewise; a father blocks siblings.
rows.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة على قوله بأن الجد أب والأب يحجب الأخوات والأخوة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ata has Ibn Abbas swear at the Black Stone that a grandfather is a father and rebuke Zayd for counting a son’s son as a son but not a father’s father as a father.
rows.anchor: ما روى عطاء عن ابن عباس أنه قال : من شاء لاعنته عند الحجر الأسود ، إن الجد أب

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Shafi‘i rejects the equation: because the verse distinguishes Jacob from Abraham’s sons, a grandfather’s upward relation cannot make him literally a father if a grandson is not literally a son.
rows.anchor: فإن الله تعالى ما أدخل يعقوب في بنيه لأنه ميزه عنهم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: A difference in generational rank cannot explain denying the name “father” if grandfather and father share it literally.
rows.anchor: لو كان الاسم حقيقة فيهما جميعا لم يكن الترتيب في الوجود سببا لنفي اسم الأب عنه

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: No jurist, linguist, or exegete says that someone dies leaving one mother and many fathers, as would follow if all grandfathers were literal fathers.
rows.anchor: مات وخلف أما وآباء كثيرين وذلك مما لم يطلقه أحد من الفقهاء وأرباب اللغة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: If grandfathers were fathers, Companions would not dispute their inheritance; a grandmother would plainly be a mother, so Abu Bakr would not need to ask about her share.
rows.anchor: لو كان الجد أبا ولا شك أن الصحابة عارفون باللغة لما كانوا يختلفون في ميراث الجد

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: If a grandfather were literally a father, a grandson would be a son and inherit alongside the son under 4:11, which does not happen.
rows.anchor: فلو كان الجد أبا لكان ابن الابن ابنا لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubayy’s reading omits “your fathers,” but it is anomalous and does not displace the transmitted reading.
rows.anchor: أنه قرأ أبي : { وإلاه * إبراهيم } بطرح آبائك إلا أن هذا لا يقدح في الغرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinship words for grandfather and uncle are figurative: the Prophet called Abbas the remainder of his fathers and said to return something to his father; the ability to deny the title confirms non-literal use.
rows.anchor: أطلق لفظ الأب على الجد وعلى العم وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام في العباس : ( هذا بقية آبائي )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas’s designation of grandfather as father concerns legal status, not the lexical meaning of father.
rows.anchor: فإنما أطلق الاسم عليه نظرا إلى الحكم الشرعي لا إلى الاسم اللغوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “One God” is an appositive to “the God of your fathers,” like “forelock, a lying forelock,” or a specification meaning they intend one God.
rows.anchor: إلاها واحدا } فهو بدل { إله * آبائك } كقوله : { بالناصية * ناصية كاذبة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “And we submit to Him” can be a circumstantial clause tied to worshipper or worshipped, a clause coordinated with “we worship,” or an emphatic parenthesis of sincerity and monotheism.
rows.anchor: أما قوله : { ونحن له مسلمون } ففيه وجوه . أحدها :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That nation has passed” refers to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and their monotheist sons; umma means a group and khalat means passed away.
rows.anchor: وهم إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب وبنوه الموحدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Learning about their Islam and invitation to Islam benefits the addressees only if they act as their forebears did; merely knowing their story earns no benefit.
rows.anchor: فليس لكم نفع في سيرتهم دون أن تفعلوا ما فعلوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes imitation: each person’s deeds belong to that person, so Jacob’s family history prompts evidence and recognition of the truth, not blind following.
rows.anchor: لأن قوله : { لها ما كسبت } يدل على أن كسب كل أحد يختص به ولا ينتفع به غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage encourages faith and following Muhammad while warning against opposing him.
rows.anchor: الآية دالة على ترغيبهم في الإيمان ، واتباع محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children do not earn reward from parents’ obedience, contrary to Jewish reliance on ancestral virtue; the Prophet tells his relatives to bring deeds, not lineage, and other verses affirm individual accountability.
rows.anchor: ائتوني يوم القيامة بأعمالكم لا بأنسابكم فإني لا أغني عنكم من الله شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the belief that descendants are punished for their ancestors’ unbelief; Jews claimed the fire would touch them only for the days their ancestors worshipped the calf.
rows.anchor: وكان اليهود يقولون : إنهم يعذبون في النار لكفر آبائهم باتخاذ العجل

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: Sunnis agree that human acquisition does not mean human power creates an accident from nonexistence; they offer three explanations of acquisition.
rows.anchor: اتفقوا على أنه ليس معنى كون العبد مكتسبا دخول شيء من الأعراض بقدرته من العدم إلى الوجود

rows.speaker: الأشعري
rows.claim: Al-Ash‘ari says contingent power relates to an act without affecting it; God creates both the power and act, and the act so related to contingent power is acquisition.
rows.anchor: أن القدرة صفة متعلقة بالمقدور من غير تأثير القدرة في المقدور

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الباقلاني
rows.claim: Al-Baqillani says God creates the act’s essence while contingent human power gives it the description of obedience or disobedience.
rows.anchor: أن ذات الفعل توجد بقدرة الله تعالى ، ثم يحصل لذلك الفعل وصف كونه طاعة أو معصية

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق الأسفرايني
rows.claim: Al-Isfarayini says an act occurs through eternal and contingent powers together, like an act performed with God’s assistance.
rows.anchor: أن القدرة الحادثة والقدرة القديمة ، إذا تعلقتا بمقدور واحد وقع المقدور بهما

rows.speaker: إمام الحرمين
rows.claim: Juwayni’s Nizamiyya position says power together with motive necessitates the act: God creates by setting its causes, while human power and motive make the servant its acquirer; Abu al-Husayn al-Basri is close to this view.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب إمام الحرمين رحمه الله تعالى اختاره في الكتاب الذي سماه بالنظامية

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The other Mu‘tazilite group says power and motive do not necessitate action: a person can genuinely choose to act or refrain.
rows.anchor: القدرة مع الداعي لا توجب الفعل ، بل العبد قادر على الفعل والترك

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that if God creates an act in someone, the person cannot refrain, and if He does not create it, the person cannot do it; either way, choice disappears.
rows.anchor: فإذا خلقه فيه : استحال من العبد أن لا يتصف في ذلك الوقت بذلك الفعل

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that if God alone causes the acquired act, the person has no effect; if the human causes it, their view is proved, while joint causation is impossible because God’s power is sufficient.
rows.anchor: لأن قدرة الله تعالى مستقلة بالإيقاع ، فعند تعلق قدرة الله تعالى به ، فكيف يبقى لقدرة العبد فيه أثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects al-Baqillani’s account by the example of occupying a usurped house: if God creates the forbidden occupation, the person is made to perform the very act forbidden; if the person creates it, the Mu‘tazilite view follows.
rows.anchor: فهذا الشغل إن حصل بفعل الله تعالى فنفس المنهي عنه قد خلقه الله تعالى فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects al-Isfarayini’s joint-power model because God’s independently effective power leaves no effect for human power.
rows.anchor: قدرة الله تعالى مستقلة بالتأثير ، فلا يبقى لقدرة العبد معها أثر ألبتة

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: Sunnis argue that people cannot independently create acts: they do not know all details of their acts, and intended effects do not always occur, as an unbeliever may seek knowledge but obtain ignorance.
rows.anchor: أن العبد لو كان موجدا لأفعاله ، لكان عالما بتفاصيل فعله ، وهو غير عالم بتلك التفاصيل

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: If human creating were an additional, new property of an act, its creation by a human would require another creator and an infinite regress; if God creates that property, the act ultimately depends on Him, whose creating is eternal.
rows.anchor: فإن كان حدوثها بالعبد لزم افتقارها إلى موجدية أخرى ، ولزم التسلسل وهو محال

rows.speaker: علماء الأصول
rows.claim: Legal theorists define punishment as pure harm coupled with humiliation: not speaking or purifying signifies humiliation, painful punishment signifies harm, and humiliation is mentioned first because it is harder to bear.
rows.anchor: العقاب هو المضرة الخالصة المقرونة بالإهانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse prohibits concealing any religious knowledge that must be disclosed.
rows.anchor: دلت الآية على تحريم الكتمان لكل علم في باب الدين يجب إظهاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although revealed about Jews, the wording applies generally to anyone who conceals required religious knowledge and can support the threatened punishment of grave sinners.
rows.anchor: العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب فالآية وإن نزلت في اليهود لكنها عامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this life knowledge and guidance are best, while ignorance and error are worst; in the next, forgiveness is best and punishment worst, so the concealters are greatest losers in both worlds.
rows.anchor: أما في الدنيا فأحسن الأشياء الاهتداء والعلم وأقبح الأشياء الضلال والجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Jewish scholars knew the truth, the reward for disclosing it, and the punishment for hiding it and spreading doubt, their concealment amounts to exchanging forgiveness for punishment.
rows.anchor: فلما أقدموا على إخفاء ذلك الحق كانوا بائعين للمغفرة بالعذاب لا محالة

rows.speaker: عطاء وابن زيد
rows.claim: One reading takes the phrase as a rebuking question: what makes them endure the Fire by abandoning truth for falsehood? Ibn al-Anbari notes that af‘ala can mean fa‘ala.
rows.anchor: أن { ما } في هذه الآية استفهام التوبيخ معناه : ما الذي أصبرهم وأي شيء صبرهم على النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other reading is an exclamation: knowingly choosing what entails Hell makes them act as if they accept and endure its consequence; the description concerns their present life of moral responsibility.
rows.anchor: صاروا كالراضين بعذاب الله تعالى ، والصابرين عليه

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm says the phrase describes their future silence when ordered to remain in Hell; Razi rejects this as shifting a present description into the future and because the damned may cry out and plead.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصم : المراد أنه إذا قيل لهم { اخسئوا فيها ولا تكلمون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wonder ordinarily combines magnification with an unclear cause, but the word can express magnification alone; divine wonder means magnification, unlike human wonder that involves an unknown cause.
rows.anchor: البحث الأول : في التعجب : وهو استعظام الشيء مع خفاء سبب حصول عظم ذلك الشيء

rows.speaker: شريح
rows.claim: Shurayh rejected the damma reading “I wonder” in 37:12 because ignorance of a cause cannot be attributed to God.
rows.anchor: ولهذا أنكر شريح قراءة من قرأ { بل عجبت ويسخرون } ( الصافات : 12 ) بضم التاء

rows.speaker: النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Nakha‘i says divine wonder means sheer magnification; similarly, divine laughter, mockery, and cunning do not have the human meanings of those terms.
rows.anchor: قال النخعي : معنى التعجب في حق الله تعالى مجرد الاستعظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic has two forms of exclamation: ma af‘alahu, as in this verse, and af‘il bihi, as in “How clearly they hear and see!”
rows.anchor: للتعجب صيغتين أحدهما : ما أفعله كقوله تعالى : { فما أصبرهم على النار }

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The fifth argument begins by saying a quality belongs to a thing either intrinsically or through another cause, a premise for rejecting the proposed paraphrase of the exclamation.
rows.anchor: أن كل صفة ثبتت للشيء فثبوتها له إما أن يكون له من نفسه أو من غيره

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: They argue that an indefinite noun cannot serve as the subject, so the Basran analysis wrongly makes the most indefinite word a subject.
rows.anchor: المبتدأ لا يجوز أن يكون نكرة فكيف جعلوا ههنا أشد الأشياء تنكيرا مبتدأ

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: If “How good Zayd is!” meant “something made Zayd good,” the plain statement should retain the exclamation, but it does not.
rows.anchor: إذا قلنا : شيء حسن زيدا فإنه لا يبقى فيه معنى التعجب ألبتة

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: If God is the one who made Zayd, the sun, moon, and world good, He should be referred to by “who,” not “what”; yet “who made Zayd good” is not an exclamation.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز التعبير عنه بما وإن جاز ذلك لكن التعبير عنه سبحانه بمن أولى

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Basran parsing would make “How good Zayd is!” no different from an ordinary clause such as “Zayd struck Amr,” which has no exclamatory force.
rows.anchor: لا فرق بين قوله : ما أحسن زيدا وبين قوله زيدا ضرب عمرا

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: Knowledge that something made Zayd good is necessary, while recognizing an object of wonder is not; thus the proposed paraphrase lacks the exclamation’s meaning.
rows.anchor: فإذن العلم بأن شيئا صيره حسنا علم ضروري والعلم بكونه متعجبا منه غير ضروري

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: Their analogy with “a man is writer” is uninformative: everyone knows that some man writes and some cause made Zayd good, so the sentence adds nothing.
rows.anchor: أن في الدنيا رجلا كاتبا فلا يكون هذا الكلام مفيدا

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The diminutive associated with nouns occurs with ma af‘alahu; if such forms are incompatible with verbs, the formula is not verbal, but if compatible, diminutives should apply to verbs generally, which they do not.
rows.anchor: دخول التصغير الذي هو من خاصية الأسماء في قولك : ما أحسن زيدا
